research_question: Among people with cancer receiving anticancer therapy, what is the effect of resistance training, compared with no training, on cancer-related fatigue measured at 12 weeks or less?
control_label: No training during anticancer therapy (including usual care, wait-list, or attention control without structured exercise)
outcome_description: Cancer-related fatigue assessed with any validated self-report, clinician-rated, or performance-linked fatigue instrument at an assessment time of 12 weeks or less. If multiple eligible measurements are reported within this window, prespecify a hierarchy to avoid double-counting (prefer the time point closest to 12 weeks, then the study-designated primary fatigue instrument). Fatigue outcomes measured after 12 weeks are not eligible for this analysis.
positive_direction: A positive standardized mean difference means that resistance training reduced cancer-related fatigue compared with no training.
search_queries: cancer resistance training fatigue controlled trial
oncology strength exercise fatigue quantitative comparison
anticancer therapy resistance exercise fatigue intervention
inclusion_criteria: Original empirical studies of people with any cancer type receiving anticancer therapy that evaluate a resistance-training intervention, whether resistance training is delivered alone or as a clearly identifiable component of a broader program
Studies with a no-training comparator, including usual care, wait-list, or an attention control without structured exercise
Studies reporting cancer-related fatigue at 12 weeks or less with quantitative data sufficient, directly or after author contact or standard conversion, to calculate an effect size
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study; systematic reviews, meta-analyses, editorials, opinion pieces, protocols without results, and theoretical papers are excluded
No comparison between a resistance-training treatment condition and a no-training control condition
No quantitative fatigue outcome data capable of producing an effect size, such as means and standard deviations, t/F-values, proportions, or odds ratios

Completely unrelated to resistance training during anticancer therapy, cancer-related fatigue, or people with cancer; fatigue measurements taken only after 12 weeks are also ineligible for this analysis
moderators_to_extract: Resistance-training dose and characteristics (frequency, intensity, duration, supervision, and resistance-only versus multicomponent program)
Fatigue instrument and assessment time within the 12-week window
Participant age, sex distribution, and baseline fatigue severity
effect_size_note: Pool standardized mean differences across fatigue instruments. Orient all scales so that positive effects favor resistance training despite higher raw fatigue scores indicating worse fatigue; use Hedges-corrected standardized effects where supported by the analysis software. For multi-arm studies, avoid double-counting shared controls by combining eligible intervention arms or appropriately splitting/modeling the shared comparator. Use one eligible fatigue effect per independent sample in the primary pool, following the prespecified time-point and instrument hierarchy.
